summary: This resolution establishes House floor procedures for debating and amending two FY2026 consolidated appropriations bills (H.R. 7148 and H.R. 7147), directs the Clerk to merge additional divisions from other passed bills into H.R. 7148 during engrossment, adopts an amended H. Res. 375, and repeals Senate data-disclosure notification rules.

scores.thoughts: This is a procedural rules resolution governing floor consideration of two FY2026 appropriations bills. It sets debate time, amendment procedures, and waivers but does not alter appropriation levels, authorize new spending, or rescind funds. Therefore it has no substantive bearing on the amount of government spending.
The resolution contains no tax provisions, rate changes, or revenue measures. It is strictly procedural and therefore has no bearing on taxation policy.
No provisions address healthcare funding formulas, coverage mandates, or market structures. The measure is procedural only.
The resolution is silent on firearms regulation or Second Amendment issues.
No immigration policy language appears in the text.
The resolution does not address reproductive-health funding or abortion-related restrictions.
While the underlying appropriations bills may contain defense funding, this rules resolution itself neither increases nor decreases defense spending authority.
No environmental regulatory or funding provisions are present.
The measure does not modify eligibility, benefit levels, or funding for entitlement programs.
No education policy or funding changes are contained in the resolution.
The text is silent on drug enforcement or decriminalization.
No sentencing, policing, or justice-system reforms are addressed.
The resolution contains no trade, tariff, or globalization provisions.
Although appropriations affect deficits, the resolution itself neither endorses nor restrains deficit spending; it is purely procedural.
No provisions expand or limit legal protections on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity.
The resolution does not alter foreign-assistance authorizations or appropriations.
No election-administration or voting-access language is present.
The measure does not address data privacy, surveillance, or technology regulation.
No labor-law or collective-bargaining provisions appear.
The resolution is silent on religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
